title: Claim-level alignment, with the claim set fixed
description: A TEMPLATE. At request time the harness replaces `user_claim_id.enum` with exactly the ids from hardening/claims.json for the prompt in hand, and sets minItems/maxItems to the claim count. That is what makes `the alignment may not mint a new user claim` an enforcement rather than an instruction: a minted id is not a token the sampler's grammar can emit, and a missing one cannot satisfy the array length. The request carries NO IMAGE, exactly as in #230 — the separation between a person's hypothesis and an image observation is enforced by the picture's absence.

user_claim_id.description: One of the ids supplied. The enum is rewritten per prompt; this placeholder must never reach a request.

disposition.description: `does_not_bear_on` (the observations are about something else) and `cannot_determine` (they are about the right thing and do not settle it) are different findings and are kept apart.

observation_ids.description: Ids from the frozen observation inventory. Empty is legitimate for does_not_bear_on; the critic requires at least one for supports and challenges, because a stance that moves the claim has to rest on something.

discriminative_explanation.description: Why the cited observations favour THIS disposition over the others. `Discriminative` is the whole point: #230's captured run grounded a sameness claim on `carved as part of the solid mass`, which is true of all carved drapery everywhere and therefore cannot separate any hypothesis from any other. The critic checks this field for exactly that.

unresolved_alternatives.description: What the observations leave open. An empty string is a claim that nothing is open, and is read as one.
